summary: Mobile responsiveness verification at 320/375/390/430/768px on the portfolio SPA. Most requirements pass, but 3 real bugs remain: (1) The page horizontally scrolls on mobile (user can scroll right by 113-140px) because overflow-x:hidden is only on body and not on html — decorative absolute/fixed background blur elements push scrollWidth beyond innerWidth. (2) The case-study modal close button does not close the modal (only Escape works). (3) The mobile hamburger menu overlay does NOT close after tapping a mobile nav link.

ui_bugs.issue: Horizontal scrolling is enabled on mobile. html scrollWidth is 460/488/495/515 at widths 320/375/390/430 while innerWidth matches viewport. window.scrollX becomes 113 after window.scrollTo(200,0) on 375px, so users CAN horizontally scroll. Root cause: body has overflow-x:hidden but html has overflow-x:visible, and fixed decorative blur divs (e.g. .pointer-events-none.fixed.top-0.left-0.w-[500px], several absolute -right-24 / left-1/2 blurs) extend past the viewport. Fix: add overflow-x:hidden to html (or html, body { overflow-x: hidden; max-width: 100vw }).
ui_bugs.selector: html, body / decorative background blur divs

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking data-testid="modal-close-button" does not close the modal (case-study-modal remains visible). Escape key correctly closes it. Likely missing/incorrect onClick handler on the close button.

Tapping a mobile nav link (e.g. data-testid="mobile-nav-link-projects") scrolls to the section but does NOT close the mobile-menu overlay. Overlay remains visible and blocks page interaction. Handler should also setOpen(false)/close menu after click.

data-testid="card-live-link-legalformat" is a <span role="link"> using window.open onClick — it has no href attribute. Spec expected href=https://legalformat.in/. Functionally opens the link but not accessible/href-verifiable. modal-live-link is correct (href=https://legalformat.in/).

action_items: Add overflow-x:hidden to html element (and consider max-width:100vw on body) in /app/frontend/src/index.css to prevent horizontal scroll from decorative blur/gradient elements.
Fix modal-close-button in /app/frontend/src/components/portfolio/Projects.jsx so click actually closes the case-study modal (verify onClick wired to setActive(null) or equivalent).
In Navbar.jsx mobile menu, after clicking a mobile-nav-link-*, also call setOpen(false) so the overlay closes.
(Optional) Convert card-live-link-legalformat span to an anchor <a href={p.link}> for a real href attribute and better accessibility.
critical_code_review_comments: overflow-x:hidden must be set on html, not just body, otherwise viewport-overflowing absolute/fixed decorative elements still allow horizontal scroll on mobile.
Modal close button and mobile menu link handlers should share the same 'close and act' pattern to avoid these bugs recurring.
card-live-link should be a real <a> tag with href for SEO/accessibility instead of a role=link span using window.open.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified widths 320/375/390/430/768. Passing: mobile hamburger visible <768, desktop nav visible at 768, hero headline visible & CTAs full-width stacked, product-thinking-node-* renders vertically, project-card-legalformat opens case-study modal (Escape closes it, modal fits viewport), modal-live-link href=https://legalformat.in/, hero-cta-resume href=/assets/Nihar_Chopade_CV.pdf (returns 200 via curl), contact-email-link mailto & contact-linkedin-link linkedin, empty contact submit shows error-name/email/message, valid submit shows success toast, no console errors on load, experience-timeline vertical & item-0 expands, skills 1-col on <=430 (visually verified). Failing: horizontal scroll on mobile (html overflow-x not hidden), modal-close-button does nothing, mobile menu does not auto-close after nav link tap. Note: card-live-link is span with onClick (no href) — spec expected href.
rca of the issue: Horizontal scroll: body has overflow-x:hidden but html/documentElement doesn't. Decorative blur/gradient divs (fixed and absolute with negative margins & w-[500px]) extend past window.innerWidth. Because overflow-x is only on body, the html element still expands and remains horizontally scrollable. Reproduction: set viewport 375x812, load site, run window.scrollTo(200,0); window.scrollX returns 113 (not 0). Mitigation: in /app/frontend/src/index.css add `html { overflow-x: hidden; }` (or `html, body { overflow-x: hidden; max-width: 100vw; }`).
